item.title: Apple Vision Pro Goes On Sale in the United States
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Apple's first spatial computer, Vision Pro, went on sale in US Apple Stores on February 2, 2024, after pre-orders opened on January 19. The headset starts at $3,499 with 256GB of storage.

Vision Pro runs visionOS and pairs Apple's M2 chip with a new R1 chip dedicated to processing input from its cameras, sensors and microphones. Its two micro-OLED displays pack a combined 23 million pixels, and the device is controlled with the user's eyes, hands and voice rather than handheld controllers.

Apple describes the product as the start of a new computing platform. The high price and the external battery pack drew criticism from early reviewers, but the display quality and eye-tracking interface were widely praised.
item.excerpt:encoded: Apple's first spatial computer, Vision Pro, went on sale in US Apple Stores on February 2, 2024, after pre-orders opened on January 19. The headset starts at $3,499 with 256GB of storage.

item.title: Nvidia Unveils Blackwell GPU Architecture at GTC 2024
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang introduced the Blackwell GPU architecture during his GTC keynote in San Jose on March 18, 2024. The flagship B200 GPU contains 208 billion transistors spread across two dies joined by a 10 TB/s chip-to-chip link.

The company also announced the GB200 Grace Blackwell Superchip, which pairs two B200 GPUs with an Nvidia Grace CPU, and rack-scale systems built for training and serving large language models. Nvidia said Blackwell can cut the cost and energy use of AI inference substantially compared with the previous Hopper generation.

The architecture is named after mathematician David Blackwell. Major cloud providers including AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Oracle said they would offer Blackwell-based instances.
item.excerpt:encoded: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang introduced the Blackwell GPU architecture during his GTC keynote in San Jose on March 18, 2024. The flagship B200 GPU contains 208 billion transistors spread across two dies joined by a 10 TB/s chip-to-chip link.

item.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-4o, a Faster Multimodal Model for Everyone
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI announced GPT-4o on May 13, 2024. The "o" stands for omni: a single model that accepts and produces text, audio and images, instead of chaining separate models together.

OpenAI said GPT-4o can respond to spoken input in as little as 232 milliseconds, about 320 milliseconds on average, which is close to human conversational speed. In the API, the model was priced at half the cost of GPT-4 Turbo while running twice as fast.

The company also made GPT-4o available to free ChatGPT users, with usage limits, giving them access to GPT-4-class intelligence, web browsing, data analysis and file uploads for the first time.
item.excerpt:encoded: OpenAI announced GPT-4o on May 13, 2024. The "o" stands for omni: a single model that accepts and produces text, audio and images, instead of chaining separate models together.

item.title: Microsoft Introduces Copilot+ PCs Built Around On-Device AI
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft unveiled a new category of Windows laptops called Copilot+ PCs on May 20, 2024. To qualify, a machine needs a neural processing unit capable of at least 40 trillion operations per second, along with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage.

The first wave used Qualcomm's Arm-based Snapdragon X Elite and X Plus processors and came from Microsoft's own Surface line as well as Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo and Samsung, starting at $999 and shipping from June 18.

Microsoft highlighted on-device AI features such as Live Captions with translation and Cocreator in Paint. Its headline feature, Recall, which takes periodic snapshots of on-screen activity, was delayed after security researchers and privacy advocates raised concerns.
item.excerpt:encoded: Microsoft unveiled a new category of Windows laptops called Copilot+ PCs on May 20, 2024. To qualify, a machine needs a neural processing unit capable of at least 40 trillion operations per second, along with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage.

item.title: Apple Announces Apple Intelligence at WWDC 2024
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
At its Worldwide Developers Conference on June 10, 2024, Apple announced Apple Intelligence, a set of generative AI features coming to iOS 18, iPadOS 18 and macOS Sequoia.

The features include system-wide writing tools, image generation with Image Playground, notification summaries and a redesigned Siri with better understanding of personal context. Most requests run on the device. More complex tasks go to Private Cloud Compute, Apple-silicon servers that Apple says do not retain user data.

Apple also announced an integration with OpenAI's ChatGPT, which Siri can call on with the user's permission. Apple Intelligence requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later, or an iPad or Mac with an M1 chip or newer.
item.excerpt:encoded: At its Worldwide Developers Conference on June 10, 2024, Apple announced Apple Intelligence, a set of generative AI features coming to iOS 18, iPadOS 18 and macOS Sequoia.

item.title: Nvidia Briefly Becomes the World's Most Valuable Company
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia passed Microsoft on June 18, 2024 to become the world's most valuable public company, with a market capitalization of about $3.34 trillion.

The milestone came after a rally driven by strong demand for its data center GPUs, which have become the standard hardware for training and running AI models. Nvidia's shares had more than tripled over the previous year, helped by a 10-for-1 stock split earlier in June.

The company held the top position only briefly before Microsoft and Apple traded places with it again, but the moment showed how central AI chips had become to the technology industry and to investors.
item.excerpt:encoded: Nvidia passed Microsoft on June 18, 2024 to become the world's most valuable public company, with a market capitalization of about $3.34 trillion.

item.title: Faulty CrowdStrike Update Crashes Millions of Windows PCs Worldwide
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
A defective content update to CrowdStrike's Falcon endpoint security software caused Windows computers around the world to crash on July 19, 2024. Affected machines showed the blue screen of death and got stuck in boot loops.

Microsoft later estimated that about 8.5 million Windows devices were affected. Airlines grounded flights, hospitals postponed procedures, and banks, broadcasters and payment systems were disrupted. The problem came from a single configuration file, and the fix required booting each machine into Safe Mode or recovery to delete it, often by hand.

CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz apologized and said the incident was not a cyberattack. The event became one of the largest IT outages in history and started a debate about kernel-level access for security software.
item.excerpt:encoded: A defective content update to CrowdStrike's Falcon endpoint security software caused Windows computers around the world to crash on July 19, 2024. Affected machines showed the blue screen of death and got stuck in boot loops.

item.title: The EU AI Act Officially Enters Into Force
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act entered into force on August 1, 2024. It is the world's first comprehensive legal framework for AI.

The law sorts AI systems by risk. Practices judged to pose unacceptable risk, such as social scoring by governments, are banned from February 2, 2025. Obligations for general-purpose AI models apply from August 2025, and most rules for high-risk systems take effect in August 2026.

Companies that break the rules face fines of up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher. The European AI Office was set up to oversee enforcement, especially for providers of large general-purpose models.
item.excerpt:encoded: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act entered into force on August 1, 2024. It is the world's first comprehensive legal framework for AI.

item.title: Intel to Cut More Than 15% of Workforce and Suspend Dividend
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Intel announced on August 1, 2024, alongside its second-quarter results, that it would cut more than 15% of its workforce as part of a plan to save $10 billion in costs in 2025.

The chipmaker also said it would suspend its dividend starting in the fourth quarter. CEO Pat Gelsinger said revenue had not grown as expected and that the company had not yet benefited fully from trends such as AI.

Investors reacted badly. Intel's stock fell about 26% the next day, its worst single-day drop in decades, as the company faced competition from AMD, Nvidia and Arm-based designs while spending heavily on its foundry business.
item.excerpt:encoded: Intel announced on August 1, 2024, alongside its second-quarter results, that it would cut more than 15% of its workforce as part of a plan to save $10 billion in costs in 2025.

item.title: Judge Rules Google Illegally Maintained a Search Monopoly
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
US District Judge Amit Mehta ruled on August 5, 2024 that Google broke antitrust law by maintaining a monopoly in online search. "Google is a monopolist," he wrote in the decision.

The case, brought by the Justice Department and a group of states, focused on the deals Google signs to be the default search engine on browsers and smartphones. The court found that Google paid $26.3 billion in 2021 alone for those default placements, with Apple receiving the largest share.

The ruling was the biggest antitrust decision against a technology company in decades. A separate phase of the case would decide remedies, and Google said it would appeal.
item.excerpt:encoded: US District Judge Amit Mehta ruled on August 5, 2024 that Google broke antitrust law by maintaining a monopoly in online search. "Google is a monopolist," he wrote in the decision.

item.title: SpaceX Catches Starship Super Heavy Booster With Launch Tower Arms
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
On October 13, 2024, during Starship's fifth test flight, SpaceX caught the returning Super Heavy booster with the mechanical arms of its launch tower at Starbase, Texas.

The booster lifted off, separated from the Starship upper stage, and flew back to the launch site. The tower's two arms, nicknamed "chopsticks", closed around it as it hovered over the pad. Engineers and spectators cheered, since the maneuver had been considered one of the hardest steps in SpaceX's plan to make the rocket fully reusable.

The Starship upper stage continued on its suborbital path and made a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean. Catching boosters is intended to cut turnaround times and costs.
item.excerpt:encoded: On October 13, 2024, during Starship's fifth test flight, SpaceX caught the returning Super Heavy booster with the mechanical arms of its launch tower at Starbase, Texas.

item.title: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger Retires Amid Turnaround Struggles
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Intel announced on December 2, 2024 that CEO Pat Gelsinger had retired and stepped down from the board, effective December 1. Reports said the board had lost confidence in the pace of his turnaround plan.

Chief financial officer David Zinsner and Michelle Johnston Holthaus, head of Intel Products, were named interim co-CEOs, while board chair Frank Yeary became interim executive chair.

Gelsinger returned to Intel in 2021 with a plan to regain manufacturing leadership and build a foundry business serving outside customers. His tenure included large losses, layoffs and a falling share price as competitors gained ground.
item.excerpt:encoded: Intel announced on December 2, 2024 that CEO Pat Gelsinger had retired and stepped down from the board, effective December 1. Reports said the board had lost confidence in the pace of his turnaround plan.

item.title: Google Unveils Willow Quantum Chip With Breakthrough Error Correction
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Google Quantum AI announced Willow on December 9, 2024. The 105-qubit superconducting chip showed that errors can drop exponentially as more qubits are added, with results published in Nature.

This result, known as operating below the error-correction threshold, had been a goal of the field for nearly 30 years. Google also said Willow finished a random circuit sampling benchmark in under five minutes, a task it estimated would take one of today's fastest supercomputers 10 septillion years.

Google stressed that the benchmark has no practical use, but said Willow is an important step toward large, error-corrected quantum computers that can solve useful problems.
item.excerpt:encoded: Google Quantum AI announced Willow on December 9, 2024. The 105-qubit superconducting chip showed that errors can drop exponentially as more qubits are added, with results published in Nature.

item.title: TikTok Goes Dark in the US, Then Returns Within a Day
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
TikTok stopped working for US users late on January 18, 2025, a day after the Supreme Court unanimously upheld a law requiring ByteDance to sell the app or face a nationwide ban.

The law, passed in 2024 over national security concerns, took effect on January 19. App stores removed TikTok, and users opening the app saw a message saying it was unavailable.

Service started coming back within hours, after President-elect Donald Trump said he would issue an executive order delaying enforcement once he took office. He signed an order on January 20 giving TikTok a 75-day reprieve while talks over a possible deal continued.
item.excerpt:encoded: TikTok stopped working for US users late on January 18, 2025, a day after the Supreme Court unanimously upheld a law requiring ByteDance to sell the app or face a nationwide ban.

item.title: OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle Announce $500 Billion Stargate Project
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
At the White House on January 21, 2025, OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and investment firm MGX announced Stargate, a joint venture planning to invest up to $500 billion in AI infrastructure in the United States over four years.

The partners said $100 billion would be deployed immediately. SoftBank's Masayoshi Son will chair the venture, with SoftBank handling financial responsibility and OpenAI handling operations. Arm, Microsoft, Nvidia and Oracle were named as key technology partners.

Construction of the first data center campus was already underway in Abilene, Texas. The announcement was one of the largest infrastructure commitments in technology history.
item.excerpt:encoded: At the White House on January 21, 2025, OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and investment firm MGX announced Stargate, a joint venture planning to invest up to $500 billion in AI infrastructure in the United States over four years.

item.title: DeepSeek's R1 Model Rattles Markets and Wipes Billions From Nvidia
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Chinese AI lab DeepSeek's R1 reasoning model shook global markets on January 27, 2025. Nvidia shares fell about 17%, erasing roughly $589 billion in market value, the largest single-day loss for any company in US history.

Released on January 20 with open weights under an MIT license, R1 matched OpenAI's o1 on several math and coding benchmarks. DeepSeek's app also rose to the top of Apple's US App Store. Investors were alarmed by DeepSeek's claim that the final training run of its underlying V3 model cost only about $5.6 million in compute.

The episode raised questions about how much spending on AI hardware is really needed. It also increased attention on efficient training methods and on the growing quality of open-weight models from China.
item.excerpt:encoded: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek's R1 reasoning model shook global markets on January 27, 2025. Nvidia shares fell about 17%, erasing roughly $589 billion in market value, the largest single-day loss for any company in US history.

item.title: Microsoft Unveils Majorana 1, a Topological Quantum Chip
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft introduced Majorana 1 on February 19, 2025, describing it as the first quantum processor built on a topological core architecture.

The chip uses what Microsoft calls a topoconductor, made from indium arsenide and aluminum, to create and control Majorana zero modes. In theory, these should produce qubits that are more stable and less prone to errors. The current chip holds eight qubits, but Microsoft says the design could eventually scale to a million on a single chip.

The company published related research in Nature. Some physicists questioned whether the results proved topological qubits exist, and Microsoft said more data would follow.
item.excerpt:encoded: Microsoft introduced Majorana 1 on February 19, 2025, describing it as the first quantum processor built on a topological core architecture.

item.title: Apple Launches iPhone 16e With Its First In-House Modem
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Apple announced the iPhone 16e on February 19, 2025, priced from $599. It replaced the iPhone SE as the entry point to the iPhone lineup.

The phone has a 6.1-inch OLED display, Face ID, the A18 chip and a 48MP camera, and it supports Apple Intelligence. It is also the first device with the Apple C1, the company's first in-house cellular modem, which Apple called its most power-efficient modem in an iPhone.

The C1 is a big step in Apple's long effort to rely less on Qualcomm for modems. The iPhone 16e went on sale February 28.
item.excerpt:encoded: Apple announced the iPhone 16e on February 19, 2025, priced from $599. It replaced the iPhone SE as the entry point to the iPhone lineup.

item.title: Apple Pledges More Than $500 Billion in US Investment
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Apple said on February 24, 2025 that it plans to spend more than $500 billion in the United States over the next four years.

The plan includes a new factory in Houston to build servers for Apple Intelligence and its Private Cloud Compute, which is expected to open in 2026. Apple also said it would hire about 20,000 people, mostly in research and development, silicon engineering, software development and AI.

The company doubled its US Advanced Manufacturing Fund from $5 billion to $10 billion and announced a manufacturing academy in Detroit. The news came as tariffs and supply chains came under closer scrutiny in Washington.
item.excerpt:encoded: Apple said on February 24, 2025 that it plans to spend more than $500 billion in the United States over the next four years.

item.title: AWS Reveals Ocelot, a Quantum Chip Built on Cat Qubits
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Amazon Web Services unveiled Ocelot on February 27, 2025, a prototype quantum computing chip developed at the AWS Center for Quantum Computing at Caltech.

Ocelot uses cat qubits, named after Schrödinger's thought experiment, which naturally resist certain kinds of errors. AWS said this approach could cut the cost of quantum error correction by up to 90% compared with current methods.

Ocelot came just after quantum announcements from Google and Microsoft. AWS said the design could shorten the timeline to practical quantum computers by as much as five years.
item.excerpt:encoded: Amazon Web Services unveiled Ocelot on February 27, 2025, a prototype quantum computing chip developed at the AWS Center for Quantum Computing at Caltech.

item.title: TSMC Announces Additional $100 Billion Investment in US Chipmaking
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company announced on March 3, 2025 that it will invest an additional $100 billion in chip manufacturing in the United States. CEO C.C. Wei made the announcement at the White House with President Trump.

The plan covers three new fabrication plants, two advanced packaging facilities and a major R&D center in Arizona. It brings TSMC's total planned US investment to about $165 billion.

TSMC makes most of the world's advanced chips, including processors for Apple, Nvidia and AMD. The expansion is meant to strengthen domestic semiconductor supply chains.
item.excerpt:encoded: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company announced on March 3, 2025 that it will invest an additional $100 billion in chip manufacturing in the United States. CEO C.C. Wei made the announcement at the White House with President Trump.

item.title: Google Agrees to Acquire Wiz for $32 Billion
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Alphabet announced on March 18, 2025 that it will acquire cloud security startup Wiz for $32 billion in cash. It is the largest acquisition in Google's history.

Founded in 2020, Wiz makes security tools that help companies find and fix risks across cloud environments. Google said Wiz will join Google Cloud while keeping its products available on rival platforms, including AWS, Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud.

The deal came less than a year after Wiz turned down an earlier offer of about $23 billion. It required regulatory approval and was expected to close in 2026.
item.excerpt:encoded: Alphabet announced on March 18, 2025 that it will acquire cloud security startup Wiz for $32 billion in cash. It is the largest acquisition in Google's history.

item.title: Google Releases Gemini 2.5 Pro, Its First Thinking Model
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Google DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Pro on March 25, 2025. It was the first model in its Gemini 2.5 family of "thinking models", which reason through problems before answering.

At launch, Gemini 2.5 Pro took first place on the LMArena leaderboard and posted strong scores on math, science and coding benchmarks. It shipped with a 1 million token context window, letting it work with very long documents and large codebases.

The model was first offered as an experimental release in Google AI Studio and to Gemini Advanced subscribers, with wider availability through Vertex AI afterward.
item.excerpt:encoded: Google DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Pro on March 25, 2025. It was the first model in its Gemini 2.5 family of "thinking models", which reason through problems before answering.

item.title: Elon Musk's xAI Acquires X in All-Stock Deal
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk announced on March 28, 2025 that his AI company xAI had acquired X, the social network formerly known as Twitter, in an all-stock transaction.

The deal valued xAI at $80 billion and X at $33 billion, which Musk said reflected a $45 billion valuation minus $12 billion in debt. He said the combination would merge xAI's models and computing power with X's distribution and data.

xAI's Grok chatbot was already built into X. Musk bought Twitter for $44 billion in 2022.
item.excerpt:encoded: Elon Musk announced on March 28, 2025 that his AI company xAI had acquired X, the social network formerly known as Twitter, in an all-stock transaction.

item.title: OpenAI Raises $40 Billion at a $300 Billion Valuation
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI announced on March 31, 2025 that it had raised $40 billion in a funding round led by SoftBank, at a post-money valuation of $300 billion. It was the largest private funding round ever for a technology company.

OpenAI said the money would fund AI research, expand its computing infrastructure and support tools for its growing user base. The company said about 500 million people were using ChatGPT every week.

Part of the funding depended on OpenAI restructuring its for-profit arm, a process that was under scrutiny from regulators and critics at the time.
item.excerpt:encoded: OpenAI announced on March 31, 2025 that it had raised $40 billion in a funding round led by SoftBank, at a post-money valuation of $300 billion. It was the largest private funding round ever for a technology company.

item.title: EU Fines Apple €500 Million and Meta €200 Million Under the DMA
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
The European Commission issued its first fines under the Digital Markets Act on April 23, 2025, fining Apple €500 million and Meta €200 million.

Regulators found that Apple broke the law's anti-steering rules by stopping app developers from telling users about cheaper offers outside the App Store. Meta was fined over its "pay or consent" model, which made Facebook and Instagram users in the EU either pay for an ad-free subscription or agree to personalized advertising.

Both companies said they would appeal. The fines were far below the maximum of 10% of global turnover, which the Commission said reflected the short period of non-compliance.
item.excerpt:encoded: The European Commission issued its first fines under the Digital Markets Act on April 23, 2025, fining Apple €500 million and Meta €200 million.

item.title: Microsoft Shuts Down Skype After More Than Two Decades
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft retired Skype on May 5, 2025, ending a service that helped make internet voice and video calls mainstream.

Users were encouraged to move to the free version of Microsoft Teams, where they could sign in with their Skype accounts and keep their chats and contacts. Microsoft also gave users the option to export their data.

Skype launched in 2003 and Microsoft bought it in 2011 for $8.5 billion. It gradually lost ground to newer apps such as Zoom, WhatsApp and Microsoft's own Teams, which became the company's main communications platform.
item.excerpt:encoded: Microsoft retired Skype on May 5, 2025, ending a service that helped make internet voice and video calls mainstream.

item.title: OpenAI Acquires Jony Ive's Hardware Startup io
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI announced on May 21, 2025 that it would acquire io, the AI device startup co-founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, in an all-stock deal valued at about $6.5 billion.

As part of the agreement, Ive and his design firm LoveFrom took on deep design and creative responsibilities across OpenAI, while staying independent. The io team, which includes former Apple engineers, joined OpenAI to build hardware.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the two had been working together on a new family of AI-first devices. Reports said the first products were planned for 2026.
item.excerpt:encoded: OpenAI announced on May 21, 2025 that it would acquire io, the AI device startup co-founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, in an all-stock deal valued at about $6.5 billion.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 on May 22, 2025, describing Opus 4 as the world's best coding model at the time.

Both are hybrid models that can give near-instant answers or use extended thinking for harder problems, and they can use tools such as web search during that reasoning. Anthropic said Opus 4 scored 72.5% on the SWE-bench software engineering benchmark and could work on long-running tasks for several hours.

The company also made Claude Code, its agentic coding tool, generally available, with integrations for popular code editors. Anthropic deployed Opus 4 under its stricter AI Safety Level 3 protections as a precaution.
item.excerpt:encoded: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 on May 22, 2025, describing Opus 4 as the world's best coding model at the time.

item.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Launches Worldwide
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Nintendo launched the Switch 2 on June 5, 2025, priced at $449.99 in the US, or $499.99 bundled with Mario Kart World.

The hybrid console has a larger 7.9-inch 1080p screen with support for up to 120Hz, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers that can act as a mouse, and output up to 4K when docked. A new GameChat feature lets players voice and video chat while they play.

Nintendo later said it sold more than 3.5 million Switch 2 units in the first four days, making it the fastest-selling Nintendo hardware ever.
item.excerpt:encoded: Nintendo launched the Switch 2 on June 5, 2025, priced at $449.99 in the US, or $499.99 bundled with Mario Kart World.

item.title: Meta Invests $14.3 Billion in Scale AI, Hires CEO Alexandr Wang
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Meta confirmed in June 2025 a $14.3 billion investment in data-labeling company Scale AI, taking a 49% stake. As part of the deal, Scale founder and CEO Alexandr Wang joined Meta to help lead its AI efforts.

Weeks later, Mark Zuckerberg announced Meta Superintelligence Labs, a new division led by Wang and former GitHub CEO Nat Friedman. Meta then went on an aggressive hiring push, recruiting researchers from OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Apple with large pay packages.

The investment led several Scale AI customers, including Google and OpenAI, to cut back their work with the company over concerns about its new ties to Meta.
item.excerpt:encoded: Meta confirmed in June 2025 a $14.3 billion investment in data-labeling company Scale AI, taking a 49% stake. As part of the deal, Scale founder and CEO Alexandr Wang joined Meta to help lead its AI efforts.

item.title: Tesla Launches Robotaxi Service in Austin
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Tesla began a limited robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, on June 22, 2025, using Model Y vehicles running its Full Self-Driving software.

The pilot was open only to invited riders, charged a flat $4.20 per trip, and operated within a defined area of the city. Each car had a Tesla safety monitor in the front passenger seat, and remote operators supervised the fleet.

Elon Musk has long promised driverless Teslas, and the launch was the company's first public ride-hailing service. Tesla still trailed Waymo, which was already running fully driverless commercial service in several US cities.
item.excerpt:encoded: Tesla began a limited robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, on June 22, 2025, using Model Y vehicles running its Full Self-Driving software.

item.title: Microsoft Cuts About 9,000 Jobs in Latest Round of Layoffs
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft confirmed on July 2, 2025 that it was laying off about 9,000 employees, less than 4% of its global workforce.

The cuts affected several divisions, with especially heavy losses in the Xbox gaming business, where some projects were canceled and studios reorganized. Microsoft had already cut about 6,000 jobs in May.

The company said it was reducing management layers and reorganizing around priorities such as AI, even as it reported strong profits and planned about $80 billion in data center spending for the fiscal year.
item.excerpt:encoded: Microsoft confirmed on July 2, 2025 that it was laying off about 9,000 employees, less than 4% of its global workforce.

item.title: Nvidia Becomes First Company to Reach $4 Trillion Market Value
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia became the first public company to reach a market capitalization of $4 trillion on July 9, 2025.

The milestone came about a year after Nvidia first passed $3 trillion, driven by continued strong demand for its AI accelerators from cloud providers, AI labs and enterprises. Shares had recovered strongly from losses earlier in the year, when the DeepSeek news and trade tensions hit the stock.

Nvidia's data center business made up the large majority of its revenue as tech giants kept increasing their spending on AI infrastructure.
item.excerpt:encoded: Nvidia became the first public company to reach a market capitalization of $4 trillion on July 9, 2025.

item.title: OpenAI's Windsurf Deal Collapses as Google Hires Its CEO
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI's planned roughly $3 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Windsurf fell apart on July 11, 2025. Within hours, Google DeepMind announced it had hired Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan, co-founder Douglas Chen and some of their team.

Google paid about $2.4 billion for a non-exclusive license to Windsurf's technology and for the hires, without buying the company itself. Reports said the OpenAI deal had stalled partly over Microsoft's access to OpenAI's intellectual property.

Days later, AI coding company Cognition, maker of the Devin agent, announced it would acquire the rest of Windsurf, including its product, brand and remaining staff.
item.excerpt:encoded: OpenAI's planned roughly $3 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Windsurf fell apart on July 11, 2025. Within hours, Google DeepMind announced it had hired Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan, co-founder Douglas Chen and some of their team.

item.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5 to All ChatGPT Users
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI launched GPT-5 on August 7, 2025 and made it available to all ChatGPT users, including those on the free tier.

GPT-5 works as a unified system: a router decides whether to answer quickly or to use deeper reasoning, depending on the request. OpenAI said the model was its best yet at coding, writing and health questions, and that it hallucinated much less than earlier models. Developers got GPT-5, GPT-5 mini and GPT-5 nano in the API.

The rollout faced pushback from users who missed older models and their personality. OpenAI quickly brought GPT-4o back as an option for paid subscribers and adjusted rate limits.
item.excerpt:encoded: OpenAI launched GPT-5 on August 7, 2025 and made it available to all ChatGPT users, including those on the free tier.

item.title: Perplexity Makes $34.5 Billion Unsolicited Offer for Google Chrome
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
AI search startup Perplexity made an unsolicited $34.5 billion all-cash offer for Google's Chrome browser on August 12, 2025.

The bid came while a federal judge was weighing remedies in the government's search antitrust case against Google, including a possible forced sale of Chrome. Perplexity said it would keep Chromium open source, invest $3 billion over two years, and keep Google as Chrome's default search engine while letting users change it.

The offer was larger than Perplexity's own valuation at the time. Google had not put Chrome up for sale and gave no public response.
item.excerpt:encoded: AI search startup Perplexity made an unsolicited $34.5 billion all-cash offer for Google's Chrome browser on August 12, 2025.

item.title: US Government Takes a Roughly 10% Stake in Intel
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Intel announced on August 22, 2025 that the US government would take an equity stake of about 9.9% in the company, buying 433.3 million shares at $20.47 each for a total of $8.9 billion.

The investment was funded with $5.7 billion in previously awarded but unpaid CHIPS Act grants and $3.2 billion from the Secure Enclave program. The government agreed to vote with Intel's board on most matters.

The unusual arrangement came days after SoftBank agreed to invest $2 billion in Intel, as the chipmaker tried to fund its manufacturing expansion under CEO Lip-Bu Tan.
item.excerpt:encoded: Intel announced on August 22, 2025 that the US government would take an equity stake of about 9.9% in the company, buying 433.3 million shares at $20.47 each for a total of $8.9 billion.

item.title: Judge Declines to Force Google to Sell Chrome in Search Remedies Ruling
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Judge Amit Mehta issued his remedies decision in the US search antitrust case on September 2, 2025. He rejected the government's request to force Google to sell its Chrome browser or the Android operating system.

Instead, the court barred Google from entering exclusive contracts for distributing Search, Chrome, Google Assistant and the Gemini app, and required it to share some search index and user-interaction data with qualified competitors. Google may keep paying partners such as Apple to be the default search engine, as long as those deals are not exclusive.

The judge noted that generative AI was changing the competitive landscape. Alphabet's stock jumped about 9% the next day, and Apple's shares also rose.
item.excerpt:encoded: Judge Amit Mehta issued his remedies decision in the US search antitrust case on September 2, 2025. He rejected the government's request to force Google to sell its Chrome browser or the Android operating system.

item.title: Apple Unveils iPhone 17 Lineup and Ultra-Thin iPhone Air
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Apple announced the iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max and an all-new iPhone Air at its event on September 9, 2025.

The iPhone Air is 5.6mm thick, the thinnest iPhone ever. It has a titanium frame, the A19 Pro chip and eSIM-only connectivity, and starts at $999. The standard iPhone 17 gained a 120Hz ProMotion display and 256GB of base storage, starting at $799. Every model got a new 18MP Center Stage front camera.

The Pro models moved to an aluminum unibody design with a vapor chamber for cooling, and added longer-range telephoto cameras and bigger batteries.
item.excerpt:encoded: Apple announced the iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max and an all-new iPhone Air at its event on September 9, 2025.

item.title: Meta Launches Ray-Ban Display Glasses With Neural Wristband
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Meta unveiled the Meta Ray-Ban Display at its Connect conference on September 17, 2025. They are its first consumer smart glasses with a built-in display, priced at $799.

A small full-color display in the right lens shows messages, navigation directions, live captions and answers from Meta AI. The glasses come with the Meta Neural Band, a wristband that reads electrical signals from the muscles in the wrist (EMG) so users can control the glasses with small finger gestures.

The glasses went on sale in the US on September 30 at selected retailers, with in-store demos required before purchase.
item.excerpt:encoded: Meta unveiled the Meta Ray-Ban Display at its Connect conference on September 17, 2025. They are its first consumer smart glasses with a built-in display, priced at $799.

item.title: Nvidia to Invest $5 Billion in Intel and Co-Develop Chips
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia announced on September 18, 2025 that it would invest $5 billion in Intel common stock at $23.28 per share. The two companies also agreed to work together on several generations of products.

For PCs, Intel will build x86 system-on-chips that include Nvidia RTX GPU chiplets. For data centers, Intel will make custom x86 CPUs that Nvidia will connect to its AI platforms using NVLink.

Intel's stock jumped more than 20% on the news. The partnership brought together long-time rivals and gave Intel another big backer after investments from the US government and SoftBank.
item.excerpt:encoded: Nvidia announced on September 18, 2025 that it would invest $5 billion in Intel common stock at $23.28 per share. The two companies also agreed to work together on several generations of products.

item.title: Nvidia Plans to Invest Up to $100 Billion in OpenAI
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia and OpenAI announced a letter of intent on September 22, 2025 for OpenAI to deploy at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems, with Nvidia investing up to $100 billion in OpenAI over time.

Under the plan, Nvidia will invest in stages as each gigawatt comes online. The first gigawatt was planned for the second half of 2026 on Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform.

The deal was one of several huge compute agreements OpenAI signed in 2025. Some analysts raised concerns about circular financing, since Nvidia's money would largely come back to it through chip purchases.
item.excerpt:encoded: Nvidia and OpenAI announced a letter of intent on September 22, 2025 for OpenAI to deploy at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems, with Nvidia investing up to $100 billion in OpenAI over time.

item.title: Electronic Arts Agrees to $55 Billion Take-Private Deal
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Electronic Arts announced on September 29, 2025 that it would be taken private by a consortium of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, valuing the company at about $55 billion.

Shareholders will receive $210 per share in cash. The deal is expected to be the largest leveraged buyout in history. EA, the publisher of EA Sports FC, Madden NFL, Battlefield and The Sims, will keep its headquarters in Redwood City, California, with Andrew Wilson staying on as CEO.

The deal needs regulatory and shareholder approval and was expected to close in the first quarter of EA's fiscal 2027.
item.excerpt:encoded: Electronic Arts announced on September 29, 2025 that it would be taken private by a consortium of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, valuing the company at about $55 billion.

item.title: AMD Signs Multi-Gigawatt GPU Deal With OpenAI
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
AMD and OpenAI announced on October 6, 2025 a deal for OpenAI to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs over several years, starting with 1 gigawatt of MI450 chips in the second half of 2026.

As part of the deal, AMD gave OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares, which vest as deployment milestones and share-price targets are met. If fully exercised, the warrant could give OpenAI a stake of about 10%.

AMD's stock surged more than 20% on the news. The agreement was a major win for AMD in its effort to challenge Nvidia in AI accelerators.
item.excerpt:encoded: AMD and OpenAI announced on October 6, 2025 a deal for OpenAI to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs over several years, starting with 1 gigawatt of MI450 chips in the second half of 2026.

item.title: Microsoft Ends Support for Windows 10
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft ended mainstream support for Windows 10 on October 14, 2025, ten years after the operating system launched. PCs still running it no longer receive free security updates, feature updates or technical support.

Consumers who aren't ready to upgrade can sign up for a year of Extended Security Updates. Outside the European Economic Area, the program costs $30 or can be obtained for free by syncing settings with Windows Backup or redeeming Microsoft Rewards points. Users in the EEA get it at no cost.

Many older PCs can't run Windows 11 because of its hardware requirements, including TPM 2.0. Consumer groups criticized the cutoff for adding to electronic waste.
item.excerpt:encoded: Microsoft ended mainstream support for Windows 10 on October 14, 2025, ten years after the operating system launched. PCs still running it no longer receive free security updates, feature updates or technical support.

item.title: Apple Debuts M5 Chip in MacBook Pro, iPad Pro and Vision Pro
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Apple announced its M5 chip on October 15, 2025, alongside updated versions of the 14-inch MacBook Pro, iPad Pro and Apple Vision Pro.

Built on third-generation 3-nanometer technology, the M5 adds a Neural Accelerator to each of its 10 GPU cores. Apple says this gives more than four times the peak GPU compute for AI tasks compared with the M4. The chip also has a faster Neural Engine and higher unified memory bandwidth.

Apple positioned the M5 as a chip built for running AI models on the device. The updated products went on sale on October 22.
item.excerpt:encoded: Apple announced its M5 chip on October 15, 2025, alongside updated versions of the 14-inch MacBook Pro, iPad Pro and Apple Vision Pro.

item.title: Major AWS Outage Disrupts Apps and Websites Worldwide
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
A major Amazon Web Services outage on October 20, 2025 took down or disrupted many popular apps and websites, including Snapchat, Fortnite, Venmo, Ring and Amazon's own Alexa and shopping services.

The problem began in AWS's US-EAST-1 region in Northern Virginia, its oldest and largest. AWS later traced it to a DNS problem that stopped services from reaching the DynamoDB database endpoint, which then spread to other services. Full recovery took about 15 hours.

The outage renewed concerns about how much of the internet depends on a small number of cloud providers, and about the risks of concentrating workloads in a single region.
item.excerpt:encoded: A major Amazon Web Services outage on October 20, 2025 took down or disrupted many popular apps and websites, including Snapchat, Fortnite, Venmo, Ring and Amazon's own Alexa and shopping services.

item.title: OpenAI Completes Recapitalization; Microsoft Takes About 27% Stake
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI completed its long-planned restructuring on October 28, 2025. Its for-profit arm became a public benefit corporation, OpenAI Group PBC, controlled by the nonprofit, which was renamed the OpenAI Foundation.

The foundation holds about 26% of OpenAI Group, worth roughly $130 billion at the time, and Microsoft holds about 27%, worth around $135 billion. Under a new agreement, Microsoft keeps rights to OpenAI's models and products through 2032, and any claim that OpenAI has achieved AGI will be checked by an independent expert panel.

OpenAI also committed to buying an additional $250 billion in Azure cloud services. Microsoft gave up its right of first refusal to be OpenAI's compute provider.
item.excerpt:encoded: OpenAI completed its long-planned restructuring on October 28, 2025. Its for-profit arm became a public benefit corporation, OpenAI Group PBC, controlled by the nonprofit, which was renamed the OpenAI Foundation.

item.title: Nvidia Becomes First Company Worth $5 Trillion
item.dc:creator: newsdesk
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia became the first public company to reach a $5 trillion market valuation on October 29, 2025, just months after passing $4 trillion.

The rally followed Nvidia's GTC conference in Washington, D.C., where CEO Jensen Huang said the company had about $500 billion in bookings for its Blackwell and upcoming Rubin chips through 2026, along with new partnerships in telecom, robotics and government supercomputing.

Nvidia's value was now larger than the entire stock markets of most countries. Some observers took this as a sign of how strong the AI boom was, while others warned it could be a bubble.
item.excerpt:encoded: Nvidia became the first public company to reach a $5 trillion market valuation on October 29, 2025, just months after passing $4 trillion.
